reviews.review:
TL;DR: Buggy and bland 1.0 launch, but somewhat fun. Would not recommend buying as of now.

The Anacrusis, a sci-fi Left 4 Dead alien styled shooter, actually isn't that bad now! However, for a 1.0 release, it is shockingly rough around the edges with no actual lore or meaningful dialogue. While general game-play is there and it is actually fun and it does offer mod support, that alone is not enough to have player-base retention. With a diminishing player-base, it is definitely not worth it's $30 price tag, let alone $10. It feels as though this is an indie title from the early era of XBOX 360 titles that you would find for a value price.

ENVIRONMENTS: The environments are actually really well made! I enjoy the colorful bits clashing with the somewhat dark situation. However, there are barely any environmental hints to show where players should go. I found myself being very confused as to where to go, alongside teammates getting lost. A lot of the newer campaigns suffer from this greatly, with actual lore and directional dialogue being tossed aside for inside jokes and unrelated banter.

SURVIVORS AND DIALOGUE: The survivors are lifeless husks, with the personality type of a coconut. The only lines you'll ever hear are severely lacking in quality, usually pertaining to some inside joke within the community Discord. The same applies for closed captions, being inaccurate and lacking spell checking.

GAMEPLAY: The game plays smoothly, with occasional dips in frame rate, but maintaining the high 50's. The weapons feel very stiff and tend to float in the hands of survivors in terms of animation, and the sound design leaves a bit to be desired due to some weapons feeling very quiet and others being extremely bass-y. I do enjoy the current perk system, but with each Matter Compiler being in a predetermined location, there isn't much variety to game-play in this regard. A lot of perks do not feel fun to use, such as weapon specific perks, while some feel like you are a god when acquiring others (healing goo LOL). The only redeeming factor is the surprisingly responsive AI, being able to quickly respond to any situation and special alien thrown in their direction. It is a great refresher from the usual AI in games being nothing more than glorified turrets. Otherwise, it feels that each item, perk, or weapon serves it's purpose, and it is consistently being balanced for player enjoyment in all game-modes. 

MATCHMAKING AND PLAYER-BASE: The servers are completely desolate. You will likely have AI teammates for almost the entire match, so bring friends or expect to be disappointed. The only time you will find a full lobby is if you are in the official Discord, which is not a good thing at all. While maintaining a close bond with your community is a great feat, it feels as though the actual average player is alienated from what the product is supposed to be, a co-op shooter than anyone can get into.

ADDITIONAL NOTES: I am appalled that the official community Discord would respond to criticism in this way, but I am not very shocked. Deletion and muting of members from your community, the thing that you pride yourself on, due to being uncomfortable with criticism is embarrassing to say the least. While we can all agree that being put on the spot when it comes to faults of your products can feel like an attack, that is not the case for this event due to it taking place in the designated channel for game-play critiques (which was archived the day after this event). If developers blocked out and ostracized every one of their critiques, we would not have the industry we have today. Doing that to a community member, of which has been a tester since the beginning of development, is appalling.

CONCLUSION: I am disappointed in Stray Bombay. I genuinely believed that this title could flourish into something great, however, it feels as if they took my money and ran off with it. This is readily apparent due to the muting and removal of members from the community for even attempting to create a valid critique. Mod support and constant banter in the Discord is great, but this alone is not enough to satiate players. I do not see this title having any kind of good reception now, not even as some sort of cult classic. I am sorry to say, but I feel as though I have been conned. This title truly took the "developers of Left 4 Dead" comment, and ran with it until it was in the ground.

If you like Left4Dead and Warhammer Vermintide AND you like aliens you'll love this game. It has a pretty good pacing and all three of the available episodes are a good length, The perks are pretty sweet, and the enemies are fun. I love this game and cant wait to see the final product.
havent played much so far but its very fun so far. i like its own unique style of co-op zombie shooter games. it can be a bit buggy at times but would still recommend

Rather mixed

L4D2 game loop, with aliens infesting a space-ship.

+: 
Interesting set of Sci-Fi weapons.
Various passive skills to choose from during playthrough.
Game play is fine.
You can ping items or location for your mates.
UI is quite intuitive and just get things done.
No obvious bugs or problems.
Bots replacing leaving players.

-:
Empty (just a wall paper) transition screen between stages, no sense/insight of current campaign progression.
Same aliens over and over.
Feels quite repetitive.
No narrative. Kill aliens between you and new escape room.
Nothing memorable apart being 10 years late.

A blatant Left 4 Dead 2 clone reskinned to be in space.  Instead of zombies, you get aliens.  The tank is called a brute, the smoker is called a grabber, the spitter is called a gooper.  The 4-player gamestyle is identical, as is the character cast and dialog.  The one-liners are less funny than in Left 4 Dead 2.  

That said, the graphics on this game are very pretty and immersive.  They mesh really well with the sound design and music.  I want to hate it for its unoriginality, but I kind of like it - just not enough to drop $15 on it.

tried it for free on the weekend with some friends, I'm glad none of us spent money on it

the game is incredibly boring, we tried it on hard and it still took a stupid amount of effort to die, the enemies run up to you, stand for a few seconds at a time and then hit you, I know it's in early access and maybe it'll get better but the enemies need to be more aggressive for it to be even remotely fun. the guns also didn't feel the greatest

I give it maybe 4.8 roentgen, kinda bad

It's Just one of those games everyone needs in they're library. Its a fun game to play and it really keeps you busy, and It's not like you will have to read a book or two to play and learn from to play.

Tried the free weekend played through all 3 offered episodes. At best, this plays like the original L4D dressed in Raypunk. At worst, it's clunky, buggy, and technically inferior. It's *pretty* for sure, but everything else is kind if lackluster and doesn't really have any punch. In its current state $30 is too much - $15 is alright, and with some polish it'll probably net you some fun hours. 

Honestly, it's tough - the game isn't bad per se, just lackluster with little to define it differently from the 4-man coop of its obvious (and superior) influences other than its aesthetic.

This is a decent game. Still in early access and in need of some refinement and polish but the basic foundation is here and its very fun. I can't wait to see where this game goes from here. Hopefully it continues to expand and improve the core gameplay features. If it can do that then it will be another great addition to the co-op shooter genre. I like what I see so far!
